parole.significato: to lead, take, show someone the way to
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *johtadak (compare Estonian juhtima (“to steer, to lead”), Livonian jū’odõ, Livvi juohattua). The base verb johtaa was rather rare in Old Literary Finnish, with derivatives like johdattaa and now dialectal johdata being more common. * (to derive): Semantic loan from Swedish avleda,

parole.significato: to fall from an upright position; to fall down, to fall over
parole.testo: kaataa (“to overturn; to pour; to overthrow”) + -ua (automative verb). Possibly already as Proto-Finnic *kaatudak (compare Ingrian kaatua, Karelian kuatuo). * (to fall (die in combat)): Semantic loan from Swedish falla or German fallen.

parole.significato: bear (large omnivorous mammal of the family Ursidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karhu, probably derived from *karhëda; equivalent to karhea (“rough, coarse”) + -u. Originally a euphemism for *okci (whence oksi, ohto, and otso). Sense 3 is a semantic loan from Swedish björn and sense 4 from English bear.

From Proto-Finnic *kuuludak. From Proto-Finnic *vottadak (compare Estonian võtma). * (to do something suddenly, impulsively, usually followed by ja (“and”)): Semantic loan from Swedish ta (och) ....

parole.significato: to end, conclude, terminate, finish, bring to a close
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *päättädäk, equivalent to pää (“head, end”) + -ttää. * (to decide, choose; to conclude): Probably a semantic loan from Swedish besluta (from sluta (“to stop, finish”)).
From Proto-Finnic *takaicin. Equivalent to taka- (“rear, backside”) + -isin (temporal distributive plural). Sense 2 possibly a semantic loan from Swedish tillbaka or English back.
